claims.text: Adjusted laser remelting with controlled preheating will reduce interlayer thermal gradients during LPBF of high-entropy alloys.
Reducing thermal gradients will minimize solidification shrinkage and porosity.
The thermal-management intervention will improve dimensional precision relative to conventional LPBF.
The thermal-management intervention will improve the mechanical integrity of LPBF high-entropy-alloy components.
Conventional LPBF without active thermal management typically produces high thermal gradients.
High thermal gradients in conventional LPBF lead to dimensional inaccuracies.
Conventional LPBF high-entropy-alloy parts commonly contain porosity and hot cracks.
Defects in conventionally produced LPBF high-entropy alloys compromise mechanical properties.
The proposed intervention combines an adjusted laser-remelting step, controlled preheating, optimized scan parameters, and active build-plate temperature control.
The intervention is intended for LPBF under ambient atmosphere with energy and preheat settings tailored to the high-entropy alloy.
Reduced interlayer thermal gradients will minimize residual stresses.
Controlled preheating and remelting homogenize layer temperatures.
More homogeneous layer temperatures decrease thermal stress.
Controlled preheating and remelting prevent localized overheating during layer deposition.
The intervention will produce finer and more uniform microstructures.
The intervention will reduce fabrication-induced defect density relative to conventional LPBF.
The intervention will improve yield strength and ductility relative to conventional LPBF.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on the selected process conditions.
The benefits are expected to hold under controlled ambient conditions for standardized part geometries.
The effectiveness may diminish for extremely complex geometries or very large builds.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for optimizing or adjusting laser scan parameters, but the comparative experiment states that laser power and scan speed are held constant. The design does not clarify which remelting parameters differ between groups, making implementation of the stated intervention internally ambiguous.
